## What the chronicles say [Record]
In autumn 1381 (sources vary between August and December; the Order's raids that spring had tipped the Trakai duke) [Kęstutis](../characters/kestutis.qmd) learned of the secret treaty of [Dovydiškės](ev_dovydiskes.qmd). The English Wikipedia names Kuno von Liebenstein, komtur of Osterode, as the informant; the saga's canon has [Günther von Hohenstein](../characters/hohenstein.qmd) (verify; the Order's commanders are poorly documented). Vytautas denied knowing. While [Jogaila](../characters/jogaila.qmd) was putting down the rebellion in Polotsk, Kęstutis took Vilnius and was proclaimed Grand Duke; Jogaila was captured on his way back, swore loyalty, and was released with Krėva and Vitebsk. The sources are the Order's chroniclers (Wigand of Marburg) and later Lithuanian chronicles.

## What really happened [Saga]
Hohenstein, who owed his life to Kęstutis's honesty at the 1361 ford and the Marienburg meals (Book VI), warns him. Kęstutis arrives at the gates, finds them deliberately unbarred, finds Jogaila nearly alone in the Lower Castle sweating, and finds the Dovydiškės parchment under his blanket. He spares him: "Kraujas yra kraujas." This is his tragic hinge: the mercy that will kill him in 1382.

## Consequences
Caused by [Dovydiškės](ev_dovydiskes.qmd); leads to [Jogaila's retaking of Vilnius](ev_vilnius_retaken.qmd).

## Dramatisation
Book I ch. 1 "Senasis Šernas" (Kęstutis recalls it in Trakai, late summer 1382). The 1361 root is Book VI ch. 16–18 (Hohenstein serving at Marienburg).
